headline: COLOMBIA SILVER BONANZA — Royal Road Hits 651 g/t Ag Over 4m; Margaritas Opens Antimony-Silver Target in GAM Porphyry District
snippet: Royal Road Minerals (TSXV: RYR) announced June 9 results from its first exploratory diamond drilling program at the Margaritas target within its Güíntar-Aleman-Margaritas (GAM) gold-copper-silver project in Antioquia, Colombia — returning 4 metres at 651 g/t silver and 0.47% antimony (equivalent to 11.3 g/t AuEq) from hole MAR-DD-002, plus 5 metres at 377 g/t silver and 0.28% antimony in MAR-DD-003. The four-hole, 1,154-metre scout program identified a broad polymetallic hydrothermal system in breccia and stockwork zones carrying high-grade silver-antimony mineralization; Margaritas sits 4 km south of Royal Road's Güíntar porphyry discovery, expanding the scale of a district the company is building toward a resource delineation decision. Antimony is a U.S.-designated critical mineral with no domestic primary production.

headline: GOLD ERASES 2026 — $4,300 Wipes Out Year's Gains; Goldman Drops Rate-Cut Forecast But Holds $5,400 Target Into Wednesday CPI
snippet: Gold fell through $4,300 on June 10, erasing all year-to-date gains for the first time since early January, as Goldman Sachs formally abandoned its 2026 Federal Reserve rate-cut forecast and pushed the first expected cut to June 2027 — while simultaneously keeping its year-end gold price target at $5,400 per ounce, citing structural central bank demand it argues is rate-uncorrelated. That split position — Goldman as simultaneously the most hawkish voice on U.S. rates and the most bullish on gold among major Wall Street banks — is creating significant uncertainty in miner positioning ahead of Wednesday's May CPI print, where the consensus expects a 4.2% year-over-year reading that, if confirmed, would sharply raise the probability of an outright Fed rate hike by year-end.

headline: MOUNT MILLIGAN'S NEIGHBOUR DRILLS — Red Canyon Turns Rigs on Osiris Copper-Gold Porphyry 35km From Centerra's BC Mine
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Red Canyon Resources
snippet: Red Canyon Resources Ltd. (CSE: REDC) announced June 8 the commencement of diamond drilling and induced-polarization geophysical surveys at its 100%-owned Osiris copper-gold project in central British Columbia — located approximately 35 km west-southwest of Centerra Gold's operating Mount Milligan copper-gold mine, one of Canada's largest open-pit copper-gold producers. The 2026 program combines a 2,500-metre diamond drill campaign at the Camp target with up to 1,500 metres of reverse-circulation drilling on multiple undercover targets, testing alkalic copper-gold porphyry systems that 2025 and 2026 surface programs identified as priority zones; IP surveys are underway concurrently to refine the targeting model before step-out holes are designed.

headline: WHISTLER GOES HOT — U.S. GoldMining Builds Drill Pads at Alaska Porphyry; First-Ever Systematic Drill Test Imminent
snippet: U.S. GoldMining Inc. (NASDAQ: USAU) reported June 9 that its 2026 exploration campaign at the Whistler Gold-Copper Project in south-central Alaska has reached final pre-drill stage: equipment and consumables are on site ahead of schedule, drill pads at the highest-priority targets are under active construction, and the drill crew is expected to mobilize imminently. Whistler is a large, untested porphyry-style copper-gold system in an underexplored region of Alaska; the 2026 program will be the first systematic drill test of the project's main targets, making assay results — when they begin arriving — a closely watched potential catalyst for a district that has not yet had a major discovery.

headline: GOLDMAN'S BASE CASE: 25% COPPER TARIFF — COMEX Already 6% Above LME as 260,000t Pre-Tariff Import Surge Awaits June 30 Decision
snippet: Goldman Sachs has moved a 25% refined copper tariff to its base case — more aggressive than Morgan Stanley's 43%-probability scenario for a 15% duty — ahead of the Commerce Secretary's June 30, 2026 recommendation to the President. COMEX copper is already pricing the tariff risk with a 6% premium over LME (COMEX ~$6.34/lb vs. LME ~$13,583/t), and U.S. traders have over-imported approximately 260,000 metric tonnes of copper year-to-date, representing 2.6% of annualized global demand. Jefferies separately raised its end-2026 LME copper price target to $13,735/tonne, calling prior forecasts 'not bullish enough' given the tightening structural supply backdrop heading into what could be a tariff-amplified Q3 COMEX squeeze.

headline: BUY, SELL, OR HOLD? — Motley Fool Dissects MP Materials After Pentagon Stake, Apple Contracts De-Risk America's Only Major REE Mine
snippet: A June 9 Motley Fool analysis examines the investment case for MP Materials (NYSE: MP), whose Mountain Pass, California operation is the only large-scale rare-earth mining and processing site in North America. The Department of War's acquisition of a 15% equity stake — making the U.S. government the company's largest shareholder — plus Apple and General Motors supply contracts have materially de-risked the offtake side of the thesis, with Wall Street consensus targeting ~$80 per share. The debate now centers on how much domestic-supply-chain premium is already priced in after a sharp re-rating, and whether the government-backed price floor arrangements deliver the earnings visibility required to sustain current multiples as the broader rare earth sector continues repricing.

headline: WALL STREET SPLITS WIDE — Gold Forecast Range Spans $900 for June; Winmill Sees Seasonal Slide While Goldman Targets $85-$100 Silver
snippet: CBS News compiled June 2026 precious metals forecasts from five institutional analysts, finding an unusually wide $900 spread for gold alone: Brett Elliott (APMEX) puts the likely range at $4,300–$4,725; Deric Ned (Ridgemont Metals) targets $4,400–$4,800 with a late-month recovery; portfolio manager Thomas Winmill (Midas Funds) forecasts a 0%–5% seasonal decline driven by reduced jewelry fabricator demand in June and July. On silver, the divergence is equally sharp: Winmill warns of a 10%–15% seasonal pullback while Goldman Sachs is targeting $85–$100 based on green energy industrial demand. The analyst spread reflects genuinely uncertain conditions — the gold market is simultaneously pricing in a potential Fed rate hike and Goldman's unchanged $5,400 year-end target.

headline: URANIUM STALLS AT $86 — Utility Spot Buying Evaporates; IAEA Board Meeting and Iran Safeguards Gap Keep Geopolitical Premium Alive
snippet: Spot uranium prices held flat at $86.10 per pound as of June 8, 2026, with China's internal price simultaneously unchanged at ¥584 per pound, as utility procurement desks continue relying on long-term contracted supply rather than spot purchasing. Sprott's weekly uranium watch flags two near-term catalysts: the IAEA Board of Governors meeting, where Iran's unresolved nuclear safeguards gap and unaccounted enriched uranium stockpiles continue to inject a geopolitical risk premium into bids; and a re-acceleration in new utility contracting agreements that Sprott identifies as structurally underway but not yet visible in spot price action — a setup the firm argues historically precedes sharp spot moves once utilities re-engage the open market.

headline: ASIA BIDS UNDER THE BREAKDOWN — Shanghai Copper Stocks Hit Year-Low; Indian Gold Buyers Step In as Physical Floor Firms
snippet: GoldSeek analyst Chintan Karnani's June 8 Asian Metals Market Update identifies a divergence between Western paper-market selling and Asian physical buying that is creating a demand floor below the COMEX/LBMA weakness: copper inventories monitored by the Shanghai Futures Exchange fell to their lowest level of the year last week, signaling resilient Chinese industrial consumption; gold physical buying in India and China is reported at elevated levels near the 200-day moving average; and silver demand tied to Chinese solar manufacturing remains high despite recent price softness. Karnani argues that the extent of the disconnect between physical Asian demand and macro-driven Western paper selling is underappreciated by traders focused exclusively on U.S. rate expectations.

headline: DIPS AND DOUBTS — GoldSeek: Bull Market Narrative Intact Despite 200-Day MA Break; Central Bank Bid and War Premium Not Going Away
snippet: A GoldSeek opinion piece argues that gold's break below the 200-day moving average — the first since October 2023 — does not invalidate the primary bull market structure, pointing to the still-active central bank accumulation cycle, de-dollarisation flows from BRICS-aligned economies, and the persistent U.S. fiscal deficit as structural demand pillars that short-term rate noise cannot override. The piece notes that gold miners such as the GDX top 25 reported record trailing-twelve-month earnings and sales through mid-2026, with price-to-earnings ratios at decade-low levels — a setup the author argues is consistent with prior mid-cycle corrections that resolved sharply higher, not with cycle tops that typically feature crowded positioning and elevated valuations.
